answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a slashable identity bond. Each agent locks collateral and receives one capped vote, so influence grows only by posting more bonds. Auditors sample identities at random and confirm each traces to a distinct principal. A clone farm must fund every fake vine it grows, stacking a mesa of collateral behind its army, and any duplicate found at the zenith of an audit burns that entire stack. The attacker pays linearly per added vote and risks losing all bonds at once, so a large fake army costs more than the rewards it could steal.
